faqs.question: What should I watch on Halloween if jump scares ruin the night?
faqs.answer: Start at Level 0: The Ghost and Mrs. Muir, Blithe Spirit and Bell, Book and Candle are all BBFC U with no content advice on their records, checked 13 October 2026. If you want a little more spook, Arsenic and Old Lace is a PG for mild threat only.

faqs.question: Which non-scary Halloween movie is actually set on Halloween?
faqs.answer: Arsenic and Old Lace (1944) takes place on Halloween in Brooklyn and is a BBFC PG for mild threat. Fun Size (2012) runs across Halloween night and is a 12 for language and sex references, not for anything frightening.

faqs.question: Are there Halloween movies with no gore at all?
faqs.answer: Yes. The nine films at Levels 0 to 2 here are rated U or PG, and the BBFC's 2024 guidelines say injury detail at PG, including sight of blood, should be brief. Clue shows occasional blood on corpses, and Death Becomes Her has some bloody aftermath, so skip those two if any blood is a problem.

faqs.question: What does mild threat mean on a BBFC rating?
faqs.answer: It means scary moments that are short and resolved quickly. The BBFC's 2024 guidelines say scary scenes at PG should not be prolonged or intense, and at U they should be very mild with a reassuring outcome.

faqs.question: Is a film rated 12 always scarier than a PG?
faqs.answer: No. Ghost Town is a 12 for infrequent strong language and Fun Size is a 12 for language and sex references; neither record mentions threat. Read the content advice line, not just the number.

faqs.question: Is Warm Bodies too scary for someone who hates horror?
faqs.answer: It may be. The BBFC rates Warm Bodies 12 for moderate violence and horror, noting zombies eating brain matter, though with little detail, which is why it sits above the ceiling of this list.

faqs.question: Is there a non-scary Indian ghost film for Halloween?
faqs.answer: Bhoothnath (2008), with Amitabh Bachchan as a friendly ghost, is a BBFC PG for mild scary moments and accidental injury. The BBFC notes some jump moments but a comic context throughout.

faqs.question: Why do some people hate being scared by films?
faqs.answer: Taste for fear varies by person. A 2024 study of 558 people found morbid curiosity predicted enjoyment of horror scenes while sensation seeking and anxiety did not, and that disgust lowered enjoyment, so gore-free, low-threat films suit many viewers better.

faqs.question: Is Addams Family Values milder than the first Addams Family film?
faqs.answer: On current BBFC records, yes. Addams Family Values is a PG with no content advice, while the 1991 film was reclassified 12 for injury detail on 30 July 2025.

faqs.question: Can I invite one person to a Halloween film night with a card?
faqs.answer: Yes. The /happy-halloween card lets you edit its closing question, up to 60 characters, to name the film, and takes about 5 minutes to make. It is a one-person page, so for a group a chat message works better.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Non Scary Halloween Movies, Sorted by an Official Fear Scale

Non scary Halloween movies are easiest to pick when a rating body has already judged the fear for you. The Ghost and Mrs. Muir, Blithe Spirit and Bell, Book and Candle carry a BBFC U with no content advice at all, and Arsenic and Old Lace, set on Halloween in Brooklyn, is a PG for "mild threat" alone. This guide places 12 films for adults and teens on a four-level fear scale built from the BBFC's own wording, with every record checked on 13 October 2026.

If you send an invite with the film, note that 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, and 38.5% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it. Below: what mild threat means, the 12 films, a table, where gore starts, and why some people never enjoy being scared.

## What makes a Halloween movie non-scary, in the BBFC's words?

A non-scary Halloween movie has a spooky subject but little or no sustained threat: ghosts, witches and haunted houses played for laughs or romance. The British Board of Film Classification gives a usable yardstick, because its rulebook defines threat separately at each age rating.

In the [BBFC Classification Guidelines published in 2024](https://darkroom.bbfc.co.uk/original/ce0ab668a4e5b93e7700a03579b138c6:bebc6c5a654b0e98882bca7014157f55/2024-bbfc-classification-guidelines.pdf), scary scenes at U "should be very mild" with a reassuring outcome, and at PG they "should not be prolonged or intense". At 12A and 12 there may be moderate threat, though horror should not be frequent or sustained, while a 15 may carry strong threat and horror.

The same document adds that fantasy settings or humour may lead to a lower age rating. That is why a comedy with a body count can still sit at PG.

## 12 non scary Halloween movies, from Level 0 to Level 3

Each entry gives the same four things in order: BBFC rating and advice, the date that version was classified, why it fits Halloween, and who it suits. Level 0 means no content advice; Level 3 means a 12 earned by something other than fear.

### 1. The Ghost and Mrs. Muir (1947), Level 0

BBFC U with no content advice, classified on 25 January 1995. A widow rents a seaside cottage still haunted by its sea-captain owner, and the ghost story turns into a slow romance. It suits a viewer who wants candlelit atmosphere with zero threat.

### 2. Blithe Spirit (1945), Level 0

BBFC U, no content advice, classified on 24 April 2003. Noël Coward's comedy has a novelist hold a séance as research, only for his first wife's ghost to move back in and needle his second. It suits fans of drawing-room comedy.

### 3. Bell, Book and Candle (1958), Level 0

BBFC U, no content advice, classified on 16 July 2002. Kim Novak plays a Manhattan witch who puts a spell on her neighbour, James Stewart. It is set around Christmas, so it suits a witch-themed night more than a 31 October purist.

### 4. Arsenic and Old Lace (1944), Level 1

BBFC PG for "mild threat", classified for video on 6 April 1990. Frank Capra's farce takes place on Halloween, as Cary Grant learns his sweet elderly aunts have been poisoning lonely old men. It suits a group that likes black comedy.

### 5. The Ghost and Mr. Chicken (1966), Level 1

BBFC PG for "mild scary scenes, comic threat", classified on 4 May 2018. Don Knotts plays a timid reporter who spends a night in a haunted house; the BBFC notes one hostage scene but calls the tone comic. It suits a nervous viewer who still wants a haunted-house night.

### 6. Bhoothnath (2008), Level 1

BBFC PG for "mild scary moments and accidental injury", classified on 29 May 2008. A boy befriends the ghost of an elderly man, played by Amitabh Bachchan, and the [BBFC record for Bhoothnath](https://www.bbfc.co.uk/release/bhoothnath-q29sbgvjdglvbjpwwc0znjy1mzm) lists some jump moments in a comic context. It suits Hindi-speaking households wanting more heart than dread.

### 7. Little Shop of Horrors (1986), Level 2

BBFC PG for "mild language, violence and fantasy horror", classified on 24 April 2003. A florist's assistant raises a plant that feeds on people, staged as a doo-wop musical. It suits musical fans, since the monster is a singing puppet.

### 8. Clue (1985), Level 2

BBFC PG for "mild language, violence and sex references", classified on 22 February 2013. Mansion guests are picked off one by one in this Cluedo comedy, but the BBFC calls the killings undetailed and unrealistic. It suits puzzle lovers who want a whodunnit, not a monster.

### 9. Addams Family Values (1993), Level 2

BBFC PG, classified on 4 June 2001, with no content advice on that record. The Addams household hires a nanny with designs on Uncle Fester. It suits teens who like deadpan humour, and the 1991 original was reclassified 12 for "injury detail" on 30 July 2025, so the sequel is the milder pick.

### 10. Ghost Town (2008), Level 3

BBFC 12, passed 12A in cinemas for "infrequent strong language", classified on 17 December 2008. A dentist suddenly finds he can see ghosts in this romantic comedy. The 12 comes from language and sex references, not fear, so it suits adults who want a ghost film with nothing frightening in it.

### 11. Fun Size (2012), Level 3

BBFC 12 for "moderate language and sex references", classified on 11 February 2013. The BBFC summary describes a teenage girl looking forward to a Halloween party, and the story runs across Halloween night. It suits teens of 12 and over.

### 12. Death Becomes Her (1992), Level 3 with a gore caveat

BBFC 12 for "moderate fantasy violence, language, nudity", classified on 11 September 2017. Two rivals take an immortality potion, and the BBFC records a head twisted backwards and a gunshot with some bloody aftermath. It suits adults who find body comedy funny; if blood is the problem, stop at Level 2.

## The fear scale at a glance: 4 levels and a ceiling

The table groups the 12 films by the strongest scare-related wording on their BBFC records, checked on 13 October 2026.

| Level | Strongest BBFC wording on the record | Highest rating | Films |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | No content advice published | U | The Ghost and Mrs. Muir, Blithe Spirit, Bell, Book and Candle |
| 1 | "Mild threat" or "mild scary" scenes | PG | Arsenic and Old Lace, The Ghost and Mr. Chicken, Bhoothnath |
| 2 | Mild violence or "fantasy horror" | PG | Little Shop of Horrors, Clue, Addams Family Values |
| 3 | 12 for language, sex references or fantasy violence | 12 | Ghost Town, Fun Size, Death Becomes Her |
| Ceiling | "Moderate horror" or "gore" | 12 | Warm Bodies, Dark Shadows (left off) |

A 12 says little about fear by itself. Ghost Town and Fun Size reach 12 with no word about threat on their records, while two other 12s cross into horror.

## Halloween movies without gore: where the scale stops

Gore and fear are separate dials on a BBFC record. At 12A the 2024 guidelines allow occasional blood but say gory images should be infrequent and justified by context, so one 12 can carry gore with no scary scenes.

Two popular picks mark the edge. Warm Bodies (2013) is a 12 for "moderate violence and horror", with zombies eating brain matter in little detail, and Dark Shadows (2012) is a 12 whose advice names horror and gore.

In a 2024 study of 558 participants who rated short horror scenes, [perceived disgust lowered enjoyment but did not change excitement](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10844225), so a gore-averse viewer may enjoy a spooky film as long as the blood stays out.

## Why some people never enjoy being scared

Disliking horror is not a failure of nerve; what a viewer enjoys depends on how much fear and disgust they will tolerate. In a 2024 study of 558 participants rating short horror scenes, morbid curiosity predicted enjoyment, while sensation seeking and anxiety showed no link, so a low appetite for horror is a trait, not a flaw.

A 2024 article by Ida Bække Johannesen of Aarhus University, in the journal [Leviathan, on recreational fear and media preferences](https://tidsskrift.dk/lev/article/view/144288), argues that frightening media which is relatively less scary and avoids excessive disgusting material draws audiences heavier horror would put off. That is the gap Levels 0 to 2 fill.

## Sending a film-night invite to one person

Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. The [interactive Halloween card with a pumpkin to carve](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) takes about 5 minutes: up to six photos, a jack-o'-lantern they carve until your word glows, and a closing question you can edit, up to 60 characters, to name the film. Its kids tone has no gore and no jump scares, the same line this list draws.

For someone you want to spend longer on, the [premium Halloween page with a voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) takes about 10 minutes and adds a 60-second voice note, up to 12 photos, an optional unlock time and a 280-character reply box. Across SubhSandesh, 90.9% of started pages are published and shared.

If the evening itself is the point, [The Invitation date page](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) fits better. It asks a question they must answer, and a yes turns into a countdown to the day.

## When this list is the wrong pick

Both Halloween pages are one-person greeting pages in English, not party invitations, so for a group a shared chat message works better. A BBFC scale is also a UK yardstick; the MPA in the US or the CBFC in India may rate a film differently, so check your own board before a younger teen watches.

No scale predicts one person. The BBFC says a U is unlikely to unsettle a four-year-old but admits it is impossible to predict what might affect any particular child, and the same goes for an adult with a specific phobia. Also, 9 of the 12 films predate 2000; for something recent, try Ghost Town or Fun Size first.
